purpose: select ONE next tactical research experiment from all evidence through Sprint 23; a research prioritisation tool, not evidence that any tactic works
scored_unit: ONE concrete next experiment of a family and the tactic it serves

G.name: generality of the tactic (computed from a published scenario count)

anchors.5: capability in at least 90% of the 50 scenarios

L.name: leverage of the tactic if the experiment's mechanism holds (judgement citing the stake)

anchors.5: can change the combat power or objective control of the whole force in most games
anchors.4: changes the effective force of most operators, with known offsetting costs
anchors.3: a local advantage for a subset of operators or situations

anchors.5: entirely from the seat's observation and legal actions, cheap
anchors.4: plus simple bookkeeping of what was seen
anchors.3: needs a belief over partially observed enemies
anchors.2: needs a model of hidden enemy behaviour

I.name: isolation of the action change

anchors.5: changes no baseline-v2 decision: acts only on units baseline-v2 leaves idle, or only with action types it never issues
anchors.4: one new behaviour for one archetype, baseline-v2's selection untouched
anchors.3: changes baseline-v2's selection for a subset of units
anchors.2: changes shared machinery (routing, ordering, the gate)

I.cap: interaction class X2 caps I at 3

M.name: measurability of the experiment's result and of the engine step it leads to

anchors.5: its endpoint is a field or record of one deterministic game
anchors.4: directly observed fields, but they need events an acting opponent produces (several per game expected)
anchors.3: needs a full-step capture plus a derived quantity or model
anchors.2: needs a new observer and an interpretation model

R.name: engine and rule risk, reversed (safer is higher)

anchors.5: listed and already executed on engine 4.1.0 with known semantics, simple parameters
anchors.4: listed and documented, never executed, simple
anchors.3: listed, but its effect is undocumented, or documented with untested interactions
anchors.2: rarely listed, or complex parameters with unknown effects

P.name: opportunity: share of the 16 H0 scenario-sides with at least one published opportunity, lowered by the basis penalty

basis.TRIGGER: the published side count is the trigger's own condition
basis.STAKE: the published side count is the harm or stake the tactic acts on; the trigger itself is unmeasured
basis.CAPABILITY: the published side count is only a listing or capability the trigger needs

leverage_cap.rule: L may exceed max_without_registered_stake only when at least one cited stake item carries one of registered_levels and covers at least min_distinct_scenario_sides distinct scenario-sides

E.name: expected information per engine session, scored on the experiment's engine step (for an offline experiment, on the engine step it leads to)

anchors.5: one session answers the increment's mechanism question with a directly observed, deterministic endpoint, the trigger is already fixed offline, and a negative result removes the family's main branch
anchors.4: one or two sessions answer it with directly observed endpoints, but the endpoint needs events an acting opponent produces, or a negative result removes only one of several branches
anchors.3: three to six sessions, or an endpoint that needs a derived model
anchors.2: more than six sessions, or an endpoint that is a score difference with known noise
anchors.1: only a scored A/B of tens of games can answer anything
anchors.0: no engine session can answer the question

C.name: cost economy, computed, used only in two sensitivity variants

K.name: engineering class of the next experiment and of the engine step it leads to (the higher)

levels.0: a reading of published files, no new code
levels.1: a new analysis rule run through an existing pinned pipeline (census, replay or timeline readers), no new observer
levels.2: a new observer, capture field or interpretation model
levels.3: a new engine-side hook, diagnostic command or candidate add-on executed on the engine
levels.4: a new framework (simulator, learning, multi-sprint infrastructure)

X.name: interaction class of the action change with baseline-v2

levels.0: acts only on units baseline-v2 leaves idle, or only with action types it never issues
levels.1: replaces some baseline-v2 actions, never a MOVE toward an objective its side does not hold
levels.2: withholds or replaces baseline-v2 MOVEs that can carry a unit toward an objective its side does not hold (the binding constraint of T9 and of T2-X1)

unidentified_semantics: the probability law of the direct-fire result-table draw (Sprint 21)
rules: the family is not excluded and the experiment repairs or restates no closed increment (its distinctness statement names every related closed increment and how the trigger and the action change differ)
a new family was admitted under the seven conditions of section 6 before scoring
its endpoint does not depend on a semantics registered as unidentified, and it reads no stopped or withheld data
the next experiment needs at most 4 engine sessions, the engine step it leads to at most 4, and its engineering class is at most 3
interaction class X2 requires the next experiment to be offline and to measure the conflict with baseline-v2's onward moves before any engine session

selection_rule: eligible candidates are ranked by the weighted score W over G, L, O, I, M, R, P with the weights above

tie band: every eligible candidate whose W is within 0.15 of the first (difference at most 0.15) competes in the tie order: higher E, then fewer engine sessions to the mechanism answer (next plus follow), then lower engineering class K
if the first two in that order are equal on all three, the outcome is FRONTIER_TIE among those equal

robustness 1: if the selected candidate is first in fewer than 19 of the 27 weight variants (tie order E, sessions, K, L, R, identifier), the outcome is FRONTIER_TIE between it and the candidate first in the most other variants

robustness 2: every judgement score (L, O, I, M, R, E) of the selected candidate and of the runner-up is moved by one point in turn (within 0 to 5, L within its cap) and the main rule re-applied with eligibility recomputed; if the selected candidate is not the winner in more than 1/3 of these perturbations, the outcome is FRONTIER_TIE between the selected candidate and the runner-up
NO_READY_INCREMENT if no candidate is eligible; otherwise NEXT_INCREMENT_SELECTED
scores are integers 0 to 5; G and P are computed from published sources, L is capped by leverage_cap, the others carry a one-line reason
the weights, the band, the tie order, the thresholds 19 and 1/3, the caps and the eligibility minima are fixed by this commit and are not changed after candidates are written or scored
sensitivity: each weight raised and lowered by 0.05 in turn, the others rescaled to keep the sum at 1
each criterion left out in turn, the others rescaled
E added as an eighth weighted criterion at 0.10 and at 0.20, the seven others rescaled
C added as an eighth weighted criterion at 0.10 and at 0.20, the seven others rescaled
eligibility is not recomputed in the weight variants; it is recomputed in every judgement perturbation

perturbation.candidates: the selected candidate and the runner-up (the next eligible candidate by W)

outcome_obligations.NEXT_INCREMENT_SELECTED: describe the complete next experiment; do not execute it; return it for the owner's approval
outcome_obligations.FRONTIER_TIE: name the specific inexpensive diagnostic that separates the tied increments
outcome_obligations.NO_READY_INCREMENT: name the smallest census or mechanism study that would make an increment ready

evidence_levels.REGISTERED RESULT: a figure or disposition produced by a registered study or census under rules fixed before it was computed
evidence_levels.OBSERVED ENGINE MECHANISM: engine behaviour observed in a registered engine session or a captured game
evidence_levels.OFFLINE ACTION COUNTERFACTUAL: what a frozen rule would have emitted on recorded states, up to its first divergence
evidence_levels.POST-HOC DIAGNOSTIC: a figure read after a registered result, or arithmetic on published figures, labelled post hoc
evidence_levels.HYPOTHESIS: a documented rule not yet observed on the engine, a conjecture or an expected mechanism
